configuration_map: No spatial configuration exists. All entities (A, B, E, M, G) are magnitudes (lengths) with commensurability and proportionality relationships. The proof operates entirely on: (1) commensurability classifications (rational, medial, commensurable in square only), (2) area equalities and ratios (rect(A,B), rect(A,E), sq(M), rect(M,G), rect(B,E)), and (3) proportional chains (A:B = M:G). No points are placed in a plane, no triangles or circles are constructed, no inside/outside or betweenness claims are made. The rectangles are areas (products of lengths), not geometric figures with spatial positions.
skip_reason: The proof is purely algebraic and proportional with no geometric configuration claims. It deals exclusively with magnitudes, their commensurability relations, area equalities, and proportional reasoning. No spatial constructions, point positions, ray orderings, angle decompositions, or inside/outside claims are made. This is characteristic of the algebraic portion of Book 10.
